deck_plan.offense: Deal immediate damage with Strikes, Bash, Thunderclap and Pommel Strike, using Trip, Bash and Thunderclap to apply Vulnerable and improve attack efficiency against elites and Hexaghost.
deck_plan.defense: Rely primarily on the four Defends and Burning Blood healing, while seeking efficient Block, Weak, or other mitigation to reduce cumulative Act 1 damage.
deck_plan.scaling: There is currently no meaningful long-term scaling. The deck must acquire efficient damage, Strength support, card draw, or exhaust-based value while first becoming reliable enough to survive Act 1 elites and Hexaghost.
deck_plan.draw_energy: The deck has no extra draw or energy generation. Three-energy turns can be awkward because Bash costs 2, so low-cost draw or cards that provide useful effects without consuming much energy are valuable.
deck_plan.aoe: Thunderclap is the only AoE and is modest, though its Vulnerable remains useful against single targets. More efficient scalable AoE would help against Sentries and other multi-enemy fights.
weaknesses: Limited defensive tools beyond basic Defends
No Weak, scaling Block, or other dependable mitigation
No card draw or energy support
Several basic Strikes dilute the deck
Bash is expensive and the deck may struggle to exploit Vulnerable consistently
acquisition_priorities: Efficient immediate damage for Act 1 elites and Hexaghost
Cards that combine damage and defense or otherwise preserve HP
Reliable Block, Weak, Strength reduction, or exhaust-based mitigation
Meaningful scalable offense such as Strength or high-impact attacks
Efficient AoE that also contributes against single targets
avoid: Redundant basic attacks or Defends without meaningful additional value
Speculative setup that does not improve immediate survival
Expensive powers before offense and defense are more reliable
Warcry unless the deck develops a stronger setup or exhaust reason for it
Cards that add dilution without materially improving damage, defense, draw, or scaling

plan_change_reason: The current deck still has the same fundamental needs: immediate Act 1 damage, reliable mitigation, draw, and eventual scaling. None of the offered cards creates a compelling strategic pivot.
